---
title: "Architecture"
---

## Layers

Each layer only depends on the layers below it.

| Layer | Packages | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Interfaces | `cli` (phase 1), web (phase 2) | input, display |
| Services | `api`, `report`, `scripts`, `ai`, `core.session`, `core.registry` | orchestration, session, reports |
| Rendering | `plot` | figures built from `Result` objects |
| Core | `core` (`Signal`, `Result`, `Param`), `io`, `synthetic`, `processing`, `analysis`, `seedlink` | pure computation and data access |

```text
src/onthesignal/
├── core/        Signal, Result, Param, Session, registry, configuration, units, errors
├── io/          miniSEED, text files, export
├── processing/  study band, mains, spectral estimation, common parameters, checks
├── analysis/    noise, lnm, sinefit, sine (SINAD/SFDR/THD/dynamic), measures, spectral
├── plot/        matplotlib renderers of each result kind, style
├── report/      Quarto report generation
├── scripts/     user scripts, batches, standalone entry point
├── seedlink/    client helpers, acquisition, real time
├── ai/          providers, tools, context (agent.md), assistant
├── cli/         console, / commands, forms, completion, display, editor
├── templates/   script_template.py, report.qmd.j2
├── synthetic.py test signals (ideal N-bit digitizer): make_sine, make_noise
└── api.py       public functions built from the registry
```

## Design rules

- **R1** `core`, `io`, `processing`, `analysis` import neither matplotlib, prompt_toolkit nor
  rich, and print nothing (logging only).
- **R2** an analysis is a pure function `compute_x(signal(s), **params) -> Result`.
- **R3** parameters are declared once (`Param`): Python defaults, console forms, help, AI JSON
  schemas and future web forms all come from the declaration.
- **R4** results are serializable (`Result.to_dict()` / `to_json()`).
- **R5** `plot_*` functions fill a figure from a result; they never compute and never block.
- **R6** state lives in a `Session` (current session in a context variable); no globals.
- **R7** long operations (acquisition, real time) run in a thread, report progress through a
  callback and can be stopped.
- **R8** every user-facing feature is registered once in the command registry.
- **R9** results carry the parameters used, the signal identities (with SHA-256 of the source
  file), the software version and the time.

## Data flow of an analysis

```text
/noise S1 fmax=50          noise(S1, fmax=50)
        │                         │
        └──── api.run("noise", "S1", fmax=50) ─────────────┐
                  │ session.get_signal("S1")               │
                  │ resolve_params: call > S.full_scale >  │
                  │   [analysis] config > declared default │
                  │ Command.func = analysis.noise.compute_noise (pure)
                  │ session.add_result(result)             │
                  └ display(result) → session.display_handler (console: rich table +
                    non-blocking matplotlib window; scripts: text or nothing)
```

## Data model

- `Signal`: float64 samples in counts, `sampling_rate`, `starttime`, NSLC codes, `title`
  (file name without extension by default), `unit`, `sensitivity` (unit per count),
  `full_scale`, `source` + `sha256`, `gaps`, `metadata`, `history`. Operators return new
  signals. `Signal.label` (`S1 · title (NSLC)`) is the label used in result titles: analyses
  get it through `analysis._common.signal_label`.
- `Result`: `kind`, `title`, `signals`, `params`, `values` (`Value`: value, unit, label),
  `curves` (`Curve`: x, y, labels, scales), `tables`, `warnings`, `extra` (rendering hints),
  `meta`. A key `k_phys` holds the physical counterpart of `k`.
- `Param`: name, type, default, unit, help, choices, bounds, `advanced`, `from_signal`.
- `Command`: name, pure function, params, number of signals, `signal_params`, category,
  `read_only`, aliases.
- `Session`: signals, results, configuration, history, display handler.
